tokyo-kyoto.ov: Two seasons make Tokyo and Kyoto a bloom-and-color destination. Sakura (late March to mid April) is short and weather-dependent, with the peak week forecast reliably only a few weeks out; Ueno Park and the Philosopher's Path are the classics. Momiji, the red maples and golden ginkgo, peak in Kyoto from mid-November to early December and in Tokyo from late November, at Meiji Jingu Gaien's ginkgo avenue and Kyoto's temple gardens.

seoul.ov: Seoul has two color seasons. Cherry blossom season, centered on the Yeouido Spring Flower Festival along the Han River, is comparable in scale to Japan's but short: roughly the first half of April. Autumn color arrives from late October to mid-November, with ginkgo avenues, Changdeokgung's Secret Garden (timed tours, book ahead) and Namsan, while the famous mountain colors at Seoraksan and Naejangsan peak a little earlier and later outside the city.

hokkaido.ov: Hokkaido has two color seasons. Furano's lavender fields reach a vivid purple peak for two to three weeks in July, most reliably around July 10 to 25. Autumn comes early here: the Daisetsuzan mountains turn red and gold from late September, the rest of the island follows through October, and Sapporo's ginkgo and maples peak around late October to early November, among Japan's earliest autumn colors.

great-smoky-mountains.ov: The Smokies are a bloom park in spring and a color park in autumn. The Spring Wildflower Pilgrimage (running since 1950) is built around trillium, phlox and lady's slipper, with over 1,500 flowering plant species in the park. Fall color follows an elevation gradient: the high ridges turn in late September, the middle elevations peak in mid to late October, and the valleys finish in early November, when this is one of the busiest national parks in the country.

rocky-mountain.ov: Rocky Mountain National Park has two color windows. Alpine tundra above treeline bursts into a short, intense wildflower season in July and early August once the snow clears, narrower and later than lower-elevation Rockies destinations. In autumn the aspen turn gold, usually in the second half of September at lower and middle elevations, with Trail Ridge Road giving access until snow closes it.

north-cascades.ov: The North Cascades are a mountain-meadow park in summer and a larch park in autumn. Alpine meadows above treeline fill with glacier lilies, lupine and paintbrush for a short window once the snowpack clears. In early to mid October the subalpine larches turn gold, a rare deciduous conifer display, along trails such as Maple Pass and Cutthroat Pass, before early snow closes the high country.

swissalps.ov: The Swiss Alps offer a reliable summer display of alpine meadow flowers once the snow clears, a broad seasonal show rather than one named event. In autumn the larch forests turn gold, typically from mid to late October, most famously in the Engadin valley, while the Lavaux vineyards above Lake Geneva turn in late October and November.

dolomites.ov: The Dolomites have a bloom season and a larch season. Alpe di Siusi, Europe's largest high alpine pasture, hosts over 800 wildflower species, with soldanella, alpine poppy, arnica and edelweiss peaking in June and July and higher trails flowering into early August. In autumn the larch forests turn gold, typically from mid-October into early November, glowing against the pale rock.

napa.ov: Napa and Sonoma have a winter bloom and an autumn color season. Vintners sow mustard between the vines each winter, and the bright yellow fields have become their own local season, with a Mustard Celebration through February and March; the most expansive bloom is typically mid-February. In autumn the vine leaves turn gold and red after harvest, usually from late October into mid-November.

douro-valley-porto.ov: The Douro Valley has a spring bloom and an autumn color season. The terraced hillsides carry an official Almond Blossom Route, a brief event of two to three weeks from late February into early March. In autumn, after the harvest in September and October, the terraced vines turn red and gold, typically strongest in late October and November, often the more dramatic of the two against the river.

tasmania.ov: Tasmania's wildflowers, including waratahs, flannel flowers and endemic alpine species in the highlands, follow the Southern Hemisphere calendar and build through the austral spring into early summer. Autumn brings a rarer treat: Australia's only native winter-deciduous tree, the fagus, turns gold and orange in the highlands around Cradle Mountain, typically in late April.

lake-district.ov: The Lake District's two seasons are the daffodils and the autumn woods. Ullswater's daffodils, the ones Wordsworth wrote about in 'a host of golden daffodils', bloom along the lakeshore in spring. In autumn the oak, beech and birch woods around Borrowdale, Grizedale and the lakes turn gold and copper, typically strongest from late October into early November.

scottish-highlands-skye.ov: The Highlands and Skye have a heather season and an autumn color season. The late-summer heather bloom turns the hillsides purple, a widely photographed seasonal event peaking in August. In autumn the birch, rowan and larch woods of Perthshire, Glen Affric and the glens turn gold and copper, typically from mid-October into early November.

vermont.ov: Vermont's autumn is the classic New England color season: sugar maples, birches and beeches turn red, orange and gold across rolling hills, covered bridges and white-steepled villages. Color moves south and down from the high ground, usually peaking in the Northeast Kingdom around the end of September and the first week of October, and in the south in mid-October. It is the busiest time of year, with lodging booked months ahead.

hudson-valley.ov: The Hudson Valley and Catskills turn into a long, accessible color season, with Hudson River views, orchards, small towns and day hikes an easy trip from New York City. The Catskills usually peak around the second week of October and the lower Hudson Valley follows by a week or two, often into the end of October. Weekend crowds on trains, trails and parking lots are heavy.

acadia.ov: Acadia is the rare place where granite coast, ocean and fall color meet: red maples and blueberry barrens burn crimson against the spruce and the sea. Color starts at higher elevations in mid to late September and usually peaks in the middle of October, though it has been drifting later in recent years. Cadillac Mountain, the carriage roads and Jordan Pond are the classic viewing spots; lodging and shuttles run out as the season ends.

quebec-city.ov: Quebec City and Montreal sit at the edge of one of the largest hardwood forests on earth, and autumn paints it from the Laurentians and Eastern Townships to Charlevoix. The Laurentians usually peak in the last week of September, and the Eastern Townships and Quebec City's surroundings follow through mid-October. Old Quebec's walls and the Saint Lawrence make a rare city backdrop for it.

nova-scotia.ov: Nova Scotia's Cabot Trail turns the Cape Breton Highlands into one of Canada's great color drives, with red and sugar maples, golden birch and dark spruce above the Atlantic. Color typically peaks in the first half of October in Cape Breton, a little earlier than the southern mainland, and the Celtic Colours International Festival is timed to it. Lodging along the trail sells out months ahead at the peak.

upper-peninsula.ov: Michigan's Upper Peninsula turns sugar maple, aspen and birch forest into one of the Midwest's best color shows, along Lake Superior's shore, the Keweenaw Peninsula and Pictured Rocks. The Keweenaw usually peaks from late September into the first week of October, and the Marquette and Munising areas a week or so later. Waterfalls, lakeshore cliffs and long forest drives make it easy to see from the road.

banff.ov: Banff and Jasper offer two short color seasons. Alpine wildflowers fill places like Sunshine Meadows and Bow Valley trails in July and August once the snow clears. Then in the second half of September the subalpine larches turn a luminous gold, famously at Larch Valley and Sentinel Pass above Moraine Lake, for roughly one to three weeks. Larch Valley is among the first places to turn and among the most crowded; an early storm can end it early.

aspen.ov: Aspen's two seasons are the wildflowers and the aspen gold. In July the meadows around the Maroon Bells and the high basins fill with columbine, paintbrush and sunflowers. Then in the last ten days of September and the first days of October the aspen groves turn a blazing gold against the Maroon Bells, Independence Pass and Kebler Pass. The Maroon Bells need a shuttle reservation, and timing shifts with drought and the first frost.

denali-interior.ov: Denali's tundra turns scarlet, orange and gold in a brief, brilliant fall that starts as early as the second week of August in the high country and peaks in late August and early September, with the lower forests following around mid-September. The tundra also has a short wildflower season in June and July. The park bus season ends in mid-September, so the best of the color falls at the end of it.

black-forest.ov: The Black Forest's autumn mixes beech, larch and mountain maple with dark spruce on rolling ridges, timber villages and vineyards on the western slopes. Color typically starts at altitude in late September, peaks in the first half of October at middle elevations, and reaches the valleys by late October. The Schauinsland, Feldberg and Triberg areas make easy day drives and walks.

bavaria-munich.ov: Bavaria's autumn is a golden and russet backdrop to Munich and the Alps: larches and beech turn in the Bavarian Alps and around Berchtesgaden, while the Englischer Garten and the lakes near Munich turn through October. Color typically peaks in the first half of October at middle elevations and in the city parks in the second half. It overlaps with Oktoberfest, so lodging is expensive.

chamonix.ov: Chamonix is an alpine-flower valley in summer and a golden-larch valley in autumn. In July the meadows and balconies of the Aiguilles Rouges and the Grand Balcon above the valley are rich with alpine flowers. torres-del-paine.ov: Torres del Paine's autumn is a short, strong fire-colored season, when the lenga and ñire beech forests turn red, orange and gold beneath the granite towers, usually in April. Crowds are far smaller than in the January and February high season, and the winds drop, but days are short, the weather turns cold and wet, and refugios and services start closing as the month ends.

It comes after the January and February crowds and before the town closes for winter around mid-April, so the window is short and the weather turns quickly.

queenstown.ov: Queenstown and Arrowtown are New Zealand's most famous autumn color: poplars, willows, oaks and silver birch, planted by gold miners, turn gold and red along the Shotover River and Lake Wakatipu, usually from mid-April to early May. The Arrowtown Autumn Festival is held in late April, and the drive from Queenstown to Arrowtown and Glenorchy is easy from the road.

Weekends in the park are extremely crowded; weekday mornings are far calmer.
